heading: Term or whole life, side by side (71 seconds)
name: Term or whole life: how to tell which fits
description: Term life covers a set number of years. Whole life is permanent and builds cash value; this short video compares the two, what each is commonly used for, and three questions that help you tell which fits.
transcript: Term or whole life? Here is how to tell which fits. Term life covers a set number of years, commonly 10, 20 or 30. If you outlive the term, coverage ends. Whole life is permanent. It is designed to last your lifetime, as long as premiums are paid. It also builds cash value. Term covers a set number of years and does not build cash value. Whole life is permanent and builds cash value. For the same death benefit, whole life costs more than term. Term fits needs with an end date, like a mortgage, or income until the kids are grown. Whole life fits needs that do not expire, like final expenses or a lifelong dependent. Many families use both. Ask three questions. How long does the need last? What fits your budget for the long run? And what coverage do you already have? Whole life guarantees depend on the insurer's claims-paying ability. Loans and withdrawals reduce the death benefit.
